user_measurement.verdict: the ~300 g is matched only by 2-wall settings: Bambu Studio's system default (2 walls, 5 top / 3 bottom, 15 % grid) gives 295.1 g on the current STL, 295.6 g on the v0.6.3 print STL and 296.9 g on the Oct-14 copy (x 1.32/1.31 = what the Bambu GUI shows: 297.9 g); 3 walls give 336.0 g, 4 walls 352.7 g, the project's 5-wall plan 369.2 g. So the user most likely printed with the default process, and the CAD solid (437.71 g) overstates even the 5-wall print by 68.5 g (thick blocks are 15 % gyroid inside, not solid). Settings unconfirmed -> ASK.

A_load_path.v09_new_parts: the v0.9 propulsion module with the fin-root servo fairings (fins = landing legs, hinge bosses carry the vane side load, MG90S ear screws), any EDF / tether strain-relief mount
A_load_path.why: 4 walls make every feature up to 3.2 mm (+ arachne widening: the 3.3 mm hinge-boss wall) pure perimeters: the 2.4 mm duct and fins (= landing legs), the 3.0 mm intake window band (the 1.2 mm struts broke in v0.6.0), the 3.3 mm hinge-boss wall; every hole gets a 1.6 mm perimeter ring and 0.8 mm (4 layers) of skin above / below a horizontal hole (EDF tab tap holes, tear-out 2.4 MPa vs ~18 MPa ASSUMED shear); the 1.2 mm keyway floor stays solid (6 layers <= 4 + 4); only cores of thick blocks (shoulder ring, deck, lug and pod cores) keep 15 % gyroid as in the plan

B_shell.why: 1.2 mm skins / 1.6 mm spigots need only 2 walls to be pure perimeters; 3 walls leave a 1.2 mm ring around the M3 joint holes and the board-boss tap holes; the slicer shows these parts are already ~fully dense, so the setting changes < 4 % of their mass

C_flat_plate.why: printed flat: 4 + 4 skin layers on a 2.0 mm tray / 2.4 mm piston leave 2 / 4 core layers; sandwich bending stiffness 0.992 / 0.963 of solid; 3 + 3 layers would save 7 g more on the tray (29.2 g) but its stiffness drops to 0.936 and it carries the NAV / ESC / battery loads - not proposed

D_small_keep.settings: project print plan: 5 walls, 5 top / 5 bottom layers, 15 % gyroid
D_small_keep.why: vanes (D-flat shaft = the v0.9 torque coupler), horns (removed in v0.9) and the latch arm weigh < 4 g each; lighter settings save < 0.6 g per vane - keep the plan's 5 walls

E_ground_equipment.why: not flight mass: saves filament (33 g) and print time only; it carries only the parked vehicle

not_proposed.2_walls_like_the_users_print: saves 56 g more on the propulsion module than class A, but the saving comes out of the load path: the 2.4 mm duct / fins get a 0.8 mm sparse core, the 3.3 mm hinge-boss wall and the tab-lug tap holes lose their perimeter rings; the 3.0 mm intake band gets a 1.4 mm sparse core (intake 100 g vs 127 g)
not_proposed.10_percent_infill: class A at 10 % saves 5.4 g more on the propulsion module (346.0 g) - available if the T/W table needs it; not needed for strength reasons either way
not_proposed.modifier_volumes: a 3-wall propulsion module with a 5-wall / 40 % modifier around the tab-lug band was tried through the CLI project path: Bambu Studio refused the 176 mm plate ('plate is empty') with or without per-volume settings - NOT VERIFIED; it can be set by hand in the GUI

fin_leg.assumed: VTOL mass 1.6 kg, all weight x2 on one leg, friction 0.5, stress in-layer (fin printed upright, root line vertical)

edf_tab_screws.note: a horizontal tap hole is closed above / below by top / bottom skin layers and at its sides by perimeters: n_tb * 0.2 mm and n_w * 0.4 mm of solid plastic

keyway_floor.assumed: deceleration 20 g (VTOL touchdown) / 100 g (6.2 m/s chute landing) - ASSUMED

cad_agent_instructions: mass model: printed part mass = the slicer's part grams (supports / brim removed) with the class settings above, NOT solid volume x 1.31; for the current parts use parts.<name>.slicer_proposed_part_g (or effective_density_proposed_g_cm3 x solid volume)

new / changed v0.9 geometry (propulsion with fin-root servo fairings, shortened VTOL body, groove cover, tether mount): slice each new STL with the class settings - scratchpad v09/masscal/slice_cal.py run_one (it calls tools/make_print_files.py slice_one with the overrides) - and take part_g; the fallback shell model (k 1.012, mean |error| 2.9 % on 76 slices >= 20 g, max 9.3 %) is for quick checks only

COM / inertia: keep the solid's shape scaled by part_g / solid mass; the measured G-code centroid moves the propulsion module 3.6 mm down (class A) - use parts.<name>.by_set.<set>.part_z_centroid_design_mm for upright / flipped parts if the CG budget needs it
print plan: tools/make_print_files.py applies one process to every part (5 walls / 5+5 / 15 %); the class settings need per-part process overrides (PART_OVERRIDES) - a tools change for the CAD round

do not use the user's ~300 g print as the design mass: it was (most likely) printed with the 2-wall default; the proposed class A propulsion module weighs 351.4 g; ask the user which settings were used

printer.mass_model.note: density_g_cm3 stays the FILAMENT density; part masses come from the slicer

geometry_levers_for_the_cad_agent.note: settings cannot lighten the 1.2 mm skins (already pure perimeters: avionics module 124.8 g with every setting tried); mass leaves with geometry - every 100 mm of plain 120 mm body tube is ~59 g printed; the VTOL set drops the payload module (177.6 g part), piston (29.3 g), gps pod lid (5.6 g) and latch arm (0.3 g) at plan settings; a 0.8 mm skin would save ~0.20 g/mm but is NOT proposed without a handling / joint test

open_items: ASK the user: the Bambu Studio settings of the ~300 g propulsion print (walls, infill %, pattern, supports) - or send the .3mf / printer history; the identification above is by slicer agreement only

ASK the user to weigh other printed parts (intake, avionics module, nose, tray) with their settings - one measured part (~300 g, approximate) is the only calibration point; the slicer itself is assumed exact to a few % (filament diameter / density tolerances)

the user's propulsion module is likely 2-wall: its 2.4 mm fins / duct and hinge bosses are partly hollow - fine for the bench thrust test, but reprint with class A before flights / landing on the fins

fallback_shell_model.use: only when a part cannot be sliced (no Bambu Studio); prefer per-part slicer grams
fallback_shell_model.formula: m = rho * k * (V_dense + phi * V_core); V_dense = sum_faces A_f * min(max(n_w*w*sqrt(1-nz^2), n_tb*h*|nz|), tau_f/2) in PRINT orientation (tau_f = ray-cast local thickness), capped at V; V_core = V - V_dense; w 0.4 mm, h 0.2 mm, n_tb = mean(top, bottom) layers
